attempts.raw_response: They may also give you the silent treatment, answering only in monosyllables or not speaking at all. Sulking often involves passive-aggressive comments, such as making sarcastic remarks or saying things like "fine" or "whatever" to end conversations quickly. They might also use guilt trips, reminding you of past mistakes or implying you're the problem. When you try to discuss the issue, they deflect or minimize their behavior, claiming they're not upset or that you're overreacting. This refusal to communicate constructively creates a cycle where the original problem never gets resolved. If you recognize these patterns in your relationship, it's important to address the sulking directly. Explain how it makes you feel and set boundaries around healthy communication. Both partners need to commit to working through conflicts openly rather than retreating into emotional withdrawal.

pair.human_continuation: They give the silent treatment or shut down conversations with “Fine” or “Whatever.”  They may sometimes try to guilt you by saying something like "you don't care about me" or "nobody cares about me." Whether your partner sulks out of immaturity or uses it as a tool to control you, their sulking likely means they have a low emotional intelligence. Your partner may not even be able to express their emotions to themselves. Going forward, they'll need to develop healthy self talk and/or self love habits in order to manage this problem.  Sulkers often need to learn healthy self talk such as “I recognize that I have emotional issues and I’m prepared to work through them” or “What I did was wrong and I fully own up to that.
pair.prefix: If your partner sends messages that tell you they’re upset, but they refuse to actually address the problem, then they are sulking. There are several specific verbal and physical signs that show they’re in a sulk.  They storm off, hide away, or retreat to a room. They use immature body language when they’re upset, such as pouting, sighing, crossing their arms, or even stomping. They push away comfort and refuse to reciprocate affection.

source_document.title: Deal With a Lover Who Sulks
